blog_summary: The blog post discusses the paper 'Taming uncertainty in distributed systems with help from the network' by Leners et al. (2015), which introduces Albatross, a novel membership service that leverages SDN (Software-Defined Networking) to actively enforce network partitions. Adrian Colyer highlights several key benefits of Albatross: it detects failures faster than traditional timeout-based methods, provides definitive reports on process disconnections by blocking traffic from failed processes, and simplifies distributed algorithms by converting uncertainty about process liveness into certainty. The paper demonstrates that Albatross can enable simpler fault models, such as a unique leader selection mechanism for atomic broadcast, reducing complexity compared to majority-based agreement protocols like Zab. The author notes that this work represents a novel application of SDN beyond its original purpose of network management, potentially opening new avenues in distributed systems design.
paper_title: Taming Uncertainty in Distributed Systems with Help from the Network
paper_abstract: We introduce Express-Lane (X-Lane), a novel system for mitigating interference in data center infrastructure to improve the liveness of coordination services. X-Lane follows a novel design from the ground up to achieve interactions with ultralow latency in the single-digit microsecond range and jitter in the nanosecond range, while the remaining interaction is treated as usual. To show X-Lane’s applicability and genericity we implemented and evaluated two services atop it on commodity hardware in a production environment of SAP SE: a failure detector (X-FD) with detection time under 10 µs and a Raft implementation (X-Raft) with latencies under 20 µs. We further show the smooth integrability of X-Lane services by replacing the replication protocol of Redis with X-Raft, making it strongly consistent while improving latency 18× and write throughput 1.5×.
